subject.title: [Feature Request]: Session snapshots — save and load context checkpoints (/session save|load)

question: Should OpenClaw own a first-class named session snapshot/save-load contract, and what first version should cover across slash commands, Gateway protocol, storage/retention, archive import, and branch/fork semantics?
rationale: Current main has adjacent primitives but no unified contract for restore destructiveness, retention, privacy, archive import, or fork semantics, and automation should not choose that product/API boundary.

options.title: Design core snapshot API first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define a versioned contract for named checkpoints, branch/load behavior, retention, privacy, protocol, commands, UI/CLI exposure, and tests.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical work
options.body: Let narrower resume, archive-family lookup, public fork/continue, and deterministic checkpoint-engine items proceed separately while keeping this issue as the broad tracker.

options.title: Defer named snapshots
options.body: Keep compaction checkpoints, export commands, and session fork primitives separate until maintainers decide a unified snapshot surface is worth core ownership.

recommendation.title: Design core snapshot API first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define a versioned contract for named checkpoints, branch/load behavior, retention, privacy, protocol, commands, UI/CLI exposure, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest recent product-review signal on this issue and current session-area history.
